questions.prompt: Is there a defect in how this code handles concurrent bookings and transaction boundaries? If so, mark the line(s) where it is; otherwise answer that there is none.
Two requests try to book the same open slot for different patients at the same moment. What is the outcome?
choices: Both transactions read OPEN and the later commit overwrites the earlier one
One request books the slot; the other is retried by BookingService until it succeeds
One request books the slot; the other waits on the slot row lock and then fails with SLOT_TAKEN
Both fail with a PessimisticLockingFailureException and one is retried

questions.prompt: Why is the retry loop in BookingService rather than inside AppointmentBooker.book?
choices: A retry inside the transactional method would reuse a transaction that is already failed, while a call through another bean starts a new one each attempt
Spring only allows one @Transactional method per class
Thread.sleep is forbidden inside a transaction by the JPA specification
BookingService needs to run at a stricter isolation level than the booker

questions.prompt: A patient double-clicks and the client sends two requests for two different open slots that overlap in time. Why can both not be confirmed?
choices: The unique index on slots prevents it
The overlap query locks every appointment row belonging to the patient
READ_COMMITTED isolation forbids two inserts by one patient
Each request locks the patient row first, so the second runs its overlap check only after the first has committed and sees the new appointment
